completion:
To determine the physical unit used for measuring the final calculated hydrostatic force, we need to consider the formula for hydrostatic force. Hydrostatic force \( F \) on a submerged surface is given by:

\[ F = \rho g h A \]

Where:
- \( \rho \) is the density of the fluid,
- \( g \) is the acceleration due to gravity,
- \( h \) is the depth of the fluid,
- \( A \) is the area of the submerged surface.

The units for each term in this equation are as follows:
- Density \( \rho \) has units of \( \text{kg/m}^3 \),
- Acceleration due to gravity \( g \) has units of \( \text{m/s}^2 \),
- Depth \( h \) has units of meters,
- Area \( A \) has units of square meters \( (\text{m}^2) \).

Therefore, the units for the hydrostatic force \( F \) will be:

\[ F = \left( \text{kg/m}^3 \right) \times \left( \text{m/s}^2 \right) \times \left( \text{m} \right) \times \left( \text{m}^2 \right) \]

Simplifying this, we get:

\[ F = \text{kg} \cdot \text{m}^2 / \text{s}^2 \]

This simplifies further to:

\[ F = \text{kg} \cdot \text{m}^2 / \text{s}^2 \]

Since \( 1 \text{ kg} \cdot \text{m}^2 / \text{s}^2 \) is equivalent to \( 1 \text{ N} \), the units for the hydrostatic force are Newtons (N).
